expr: (let ((a [1]) (b [1])) (list (eq a b) (eq a a) (eql a a) (eql a b)))
note: Vectors have object identity: two separate reads of [1] are two objects ((eq a b) is nil) and a vector is eq to itself. `eql' adds nothing for vectors -- it is `eq' plus number sameness -- so it answers exactly as `eq' does here, which is the claim worth freezing before kg has an implementation that could accidentally make it structural.
